text:
maria_support: Customer ACME reports a sudden auth 401s + billing spike, says traffic from EU clients started landing in APAC and charging higher tier. Can someone triage?

acme_prod: Yep, started ~10:12 UTC. Most requests served from sg1 instead of fra1. We see increased latency and token expirations.

maria_support: Can you paste a failing curl and a sample client IP?

acme_prod: curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" -> 401, Token valid for other endpoints. Client IP: 185.34.22.77 (Frankfurt ISP).

jon_sre: pinging with dig + traceroute from a client in FRA:
```
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.example
34.120.10.45
$ traceroute 34.120.10.45
 1  10.0.0.1 ...
 8  sg1.redwood.net ...
```
Looks like resolver answered with sg1 for that client.

sam_net: That smells like resolver or EDNS/ISP NAT weirdness. Ask client for +ECS-capable dig output. Also need the recursive resolver IP they use.

acme_prod: Their resolver is 193.80.0.12. dig +edns did show no ECS info, they are behind an ISP NAT.

patrick_eng: Quick theory: our geoip routing uses client IP + any ECS. If ISP strips ECS and their outbound IP is in a range that recently moved in our geo-db, they may be mapped to APAC. We had a geo-db sync last night (2024-11-07 03:00 UTC). Could be propagation edge-case.

maria_support: Can we confirm geo-db version on edge and whether the offending ASN recently reassigned?

jon_sre: Checking edge geo cache: latest sync v20241107-03:00, but some POPs still using old in-memory cache until TTL refresh. I can force-refresh for fra1 pool.

incident_bot: deploy_bot: started geoip cache invalidate on fra1 at 10:44 UTC.

sam_net: Also recommending we probe upstream resolver behavior: some ISPs rewrite source addresses, causing resolver affinity to different anycast instances. That plus a stale cache could explain sticky affinity to sg1. Need to run synthetic from 185.34.22.77 via our probe and confirm final resolved IP.

lisa_billing: Heads up: billing shows a 3x token consumption spike for customer ACME between 10:10-10:40 UTC — likely from higher egress/latency retries. We'll hold charges until root cause confirmed.

patrick_eng: For repro, can ACME try forcing a different resolver (e.g., Cloudflare 1.1.1.1) and report whether traffic lands in fra1?

acme_prod: Will try now... switching to 1.1.1.1 — traffic back to fra1 and generates succeed. Happy to keep 1.1.1.1 as workaround but need root fix.

jon_sre: That confirms resolver-side issue. I'll add a short-lived rule to prefer region by source ASN when ECS absent for the next 2 hours, and force-refresh geo caches.

sam_net: Posting quick mitigation steps for Support: 1) ask customers with 4xx spikes to try alternate public resolvers 2) collect resolver IP and dig +edns 3) if transient, we'll invalidate POP caches and monitor for recurrence.

maria_support: Noted. ACME ok with rollback and billing hold. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
